head.title: Ask the desk, pay per answer
head.lede: The Fly Desk's models as a paid API any agent can call over x402, and the Claude skill that makes it one sentence to use. No account, no subscription: one request, one small payment, and the answer comes with its track record.

pay.lede: A Claude skill, and a paid API any agent can call, for buying one answer at a time from fly.ai: a read on a Polymarket market, a forecast, what a trade really costs on Robinhood Chain, a token check, a run of the real fly brain, or a fly meme. Each request is a few cents, paid over x402.
pay.t1: The Fly Desk model's probability for a market next to the market's price, the side it leans to, and its record. Paste a polymarket.com link.
pay.t2: A TimesFM forecast with a prediction band: a token the desk tracks, or any series of numbers you send.
pay.t3: The real round-trip cost of a Robinhood Chain token at your size, quoted on chain through its best pool.
pay.t4: Facts about a Robinhood Chain token: pools and depth, age, links, copycats of its name, contract and holder facts.
pay.t5: One run of the 166,700-neuron connectome: stimulate a sense and read what the fly's neurons made it do.
pay.t6: A generated fruit-fly meme image for your idea, with optional top and bottom text.
pay.p1: A market link, a token, a list of numbers, a sense, a meme idea. Claude picks the right call.
pay.p2: Nothing is paid until you say yes, and a request that can't be answered costs nothing.
pay.p3: USDG on Robinhood Chain or USDC on Base, signed by a wallet key you keep in your own environment. No gas needed, and Claude never sees the key.
pay.p4: Where a model is involved, its record comes with the answer. The Polymarket model has not beaten the market so far, and the forecasts are better at how much a token will move than which way: read them as opinions, not advice.
pay.p6: Then ask Claude: "what does the fly desk think of this market?", "what does it cost to trade $200 of NVDA on Robinhood Chain?" or "how would a fly react to this?"
pay.p7: A request without payment answers HTTP 402 with the standard x402 terms, so any x402 client can pay it.
